featureShowcase.chartsIntro: Charts visualize your progress over time. Available types: `volume`, `weight`, `e1rm`, `reps`, `duration`, `distance`, `heartRate`, `pace`.
featureShowcase.commandsNote: **Commands** (Ctrl/Cmd + P): Create workout log, Insert workout chart, Insert workout timer, Create exercise page
featureShowcase.durationEstimatorIntro: Estimates total workout duration based on the current note's exercises.
featureShowcase.intro: Complete reference of all code block types available in the Workout Plugin.
featureShowcase.tablesIntro: Tables display your workout logs with sorting and editing capabilities.
featureShowcase.title: Feature Showcase
featureShowcase.trainingProtocolsIntro: Each set can carry a protocol, shown as a badge in the tables. Edit these or add your own in Settings → Protocols.
featureShowcase.e1rmIntro: The best estimate of each day with the Epley formula (weight × (1 + reps / 30)), from sets of 1 to 12 reps. Warm-up and drop sets don't count.
featureShowcase.presetTimersIntro: A timer can run a saved preset by name with `preset`. Tabata and EMOM are built in; edit them or add your own in Settings → Timer presets.
featureShowcase.codeBlockWorkoutSession: Follow the note's plan set by set
featureShowcase.sessionIntro: A `workout-session` block walks you through the plan of its note: one step per `workout-log` block with an exercise, with its `sets` and targets, and the rest timer of the same section. Try it in [[{workout}]].
featureShowcase.dashboardsIntro: A dashboard shows every widget, or only the ones listed in `widgets`, in that order. Use the menu at the top right of a dashboard to choose them.
featureShowcase.dashboardGridIntro: With `layout: grid` each widget takes the cells of its line: column, row, width and height. In a narrower note the widgets are packed again in reading order.
featureShowcase.trainingCalendarIntro: The training calendar shows a year of training days and how many weeks in a row reached your weekly goal (Settings → Weekly goal).
featureShowcase.importIntro: Run **{command}** from the command palette and choose the CSV the app exported. Sets already in your log are skipped, and the log is backed up first.
featureShowcase.setsIntro: A `workout-sets` block shows today's sets as rows. The grey numbers are the same set last time: tick a row to log them as they are, or type what you did. Tap the arrow for the set's protocol and notes, and a logged set to edit it.
featureShowcase.codeBlockWorkoutSets: Log today's sets row by row

tables.latestIntro: `exercise` picks the exercise and `limit` how many sets the table shows.
tables.targetIntro: With `targetWeight` and `targetReps` the table shows how close you are to the target; once you reach it, a badge offers to write the next weight into the block. `sets` is how many sets you plan: without `limit` the table shows the last two workouts, and a guided session counts them. `workout` with `exactMatch: true` keeps only the sets of that exercise in that workout.
tables.workoutIntro: With `workout` and no `exercise` the table lists every set of that workout. `dateRange: 14` keeps the last 14 days.
tables.columnsIntro: `columns` chooses the columns and their order; `sortBy` and `sortOrder` the order of the rows, here the heaviest sets first. `showAddButton: false` hides the + button and `showProtocol: false` would hide the protocol badges.

sets.lastTimeIntro: With `workout` the grey numbers come from the last time you did this exercise in that workout. Without it the block uses the note's name.
sets.restIntro: `rest` is the rest after each set, in seconds (`0` = no timer); without it the block uses the section's `workout-timer`. `targetWeight` and `targetReps` show the target, and are the hint the first time you do an exercise.
sets.restTimerIntro: The block holds every option of its rest timer, so a day's note needs no `workout-timer`: `timer.type` (`interval` uses `rest` as the work of each round, with `timer.rest` and `timer.rounds`), `timer.preset`, `timer.sound` and `timer.showControls`. ⋮ → Edit rest timer writes them for you.

releases.v3_2_0:
**Fixes.** A `workout-sets` block with `rest: 0` no longer starts the section timer in a guided session. "Last N days" is the same everywhere (charts, dashboard widgets, filters) and includes the whole boundary day. Charts group points by training day, and trend lines use one rule. "Last time" and the target wording match in the session card, the set sheet and the target header. Custom columns such as `HR` or `Duration (s)` are read everywhere. Exercise conversion no longer writes weights in the wrong unit. Protocol effectiveness follows the set order. Exercise pages with `:` or `#` in the name get valid frontmatter. Canvas export reads sections and timer lengths correctly. Timer presets and the "Add exercise block" modal are fully translated.

**Improvements.** Timer presets are picked as chips, with a "None" option; editing a block keeps a preset that is no longer in the settings. Modal buttons use the same order everywhere, with the button row always visible at the bottom. Durations are formatted the same way everywhere.
releases.v3_1_0:
**What's new, in the plugin.** When you install or update the plugin, it shows what changed, once. Open it again any time with **Show what's new** in the command palette, or **Show changelog** under Settings → Workout Planner → Getting started.

**Workout sets for everyone.** The `workout-sets` block is no longer a beta feature: it works without turning anything on, and **Insert workout sets** is always in the command palette.
releases.v3_0_0:
**A new look for every block.** Workout logs, charts, the guided session, the workout duration and every dashboard widget are now cards with the same layout, controls and menus, with clearer contrast in light and dark themes. Nothing in your notes or your log changes: the blocks just look and behave more consistently.

**Sets on your phone (beta).** A new `workout-sets` block shows today's sets of one exercise as rows to fill in, with last time's values as hints. Tick a row to log the set and the rest timer starts on its own; tick it again to take it back, with Undo for a few seconds. Turn it on under Settings → Workout Planner → Beta features (new installs have it on), then use **Insert workout sets** from the command palette.

**Guided sessions read set sheets.** A `workout-session` now follows `workout-sets` blocks as well as `workout-log` ones, takes each exercise's rest from its own block, and shares one countdown with the sets card.

**Charts** show a stats row under the chart: average, min, max, recent trend and number of sessions.

**Dashboard widgets** have their own settings in their ⋮ menu (how many workouts to list, which figures to show, the days counted, and so on).

**Example notes** now use `workout-sets` for the exercises of the example workout.
